subject: Request: SLA credit eligibility & calculation details — Auriga Systems
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurigasystems.com>
To: naomi.feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@aurigasystems.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Follow-up on 5/29 outage — credit eligibility and breakdown

Naomi —

Thanks for the summary you sent earlier. Auriga's finance team reviewed the incident digest and asked for a clear statement on whether we are eligible for an SLA credit under our contract (SLA section 4.2). If eligible, they want a line-item calculation showing how the number was derived (downtime windows, SLO weighting for the inference cluster in us-west, and any prorations for partial-day outages).

Attached: incident-digest-20270529.pdf and uptime-metrics-05-25-to-05-29.csv.

Two quick asks from our side:
- Confirm eligibility (yes/no) and cite the clause you'd apply.
- Provide a spreadsheet-style calculation we can attach to our PO/finance ticket — we need this for internal audit.

Appreciate a timeline. We need something to present at our 6/3 procurement meeting.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of IT Ops, Auriga Systems
liam.oconnor@aurigasystems.com

From: naomi.feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurigasystems.com>
Cc: ben.carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up on 5/29 outage — credit eligibility and breakdown

Hi Liam —

Thanks — we've reviewed the digest. Short answer up front: based on preliminary calculations, Auriga looks eligible for a service credit under SLA section 4.2 (Availability SLO). I'll enumerate the exact windows and the math in a spreadsheet and loop in finance for signoff.

What I'll provide by EOD Monday (6/1):
- A worked spreadsheet showing per-window downtime, total unavailable minutes, and resulting credit percentage (using the SLO formula in 4.2).
- A short memo citing the contract clause and any assumptions (e.g., scheduled maintenance vs. unplanned outage).
- A recommended issuance timeline (we generally issue credits as an invoice adjustment within the next billing cycle unless a different process is requested).

Cc'ing Ben (sales) and Marissa (customer ops) to confirm the proposed calculation and the issuance path. If Finance needs the credit as a standalone credit memo rather than an invoice offset, please let me know — Evelyn from finance will finalize that.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

From: marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: naomi.feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, ben.carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: evelyn.hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed credit calc for Auriga (draft)

Naomi / Ben —

I've put together a draft calculation (attached as proposed-credit-calculation.xlsx) and a short rationale below. Evelyn, tagging you for finance confirmation on the issuance mechanism (credit memo vs invoice adjustment).

Draft notes:
- Incident windows (UTC converted): 2027-05-29T03:14:00Z–03:47:00Z (33 min), and 2027-05-29T11:05:00Z–11:27:00Z (22 min). Total unavailable = 55 minutes.
- Contracted measurement period = 30 days (per SLA 4.2). Availability = (total_time_minutes - unavailable_minutes) / total_time_minutes. For the affected service (inference-prod-us-west) we use 99.95% baseline SLO.
- Calculated availability for period = 99.8979% (rounded). This crosses the threshold for a single-tier credit: per SLA table, 99.9%–99.5% => 10% monthly service credit on affected service prorated by impacted capacity (Auriga has 60% of their committed capacity in the affected pool).
- Proration: 10% * 0.60 = 6% credit on the monthly subscription charges tied to the dedicated pool.
- Preliminary recommended credit amount = 6% * May invoice value for the impacted service. Spreadsheet shows line-by-line.

Open items for confirmation:
1) Whether we apply any outage adjustments for KV-cache warming or rollback windows (I recommend not excluding — these are service interruptions).
2) Whether Auriga prefers a credit memo (separate line item they can track) or an invoice offset. Evelyn — what's standard and what's faster?

If we all agree, Naomi please send the calculation and the clause citation to Auriga and copy Evelyn. If finance is okay, we'll target issuance on the next cycle (June billing) with a credit memo number.

-Marissa
Director, Customer Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: evelyn.hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aurigasystems.com>, naomi.feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: ben.carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, marissa.cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, finance@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on 5/29 outage — credit eligibility and breakdown

Liam —

Thanks for your patience. Naomi / Marissa shared the full calc; attached is the same spreadsheet with the finance fields filled (proposed-credit-calculation.xlsx). Summary below for your procurement/audit ticket:

- Eligibility: Yes. Clause: SLA 4.2 (Availability). Assumptions: outage periods are unplanned (no scheduled maintenance), and impacted capacity assessment is based on committed pool assignment as of 2027-05-01.
- Calculation summary: Total downtime = 55 minutes in the 30-day measurement window = Availability 99.8979% => maps to the 10% tier in SLA credit table. Auriga's impacted share of the pool = 60% => prorated credit = 6% of the monthly charges for the affected service.
- Proposed remediation instrument: Credit memo CM-2027-0610-AUR for $X. (We will compute the exact dollar amount after Auriga confirms the May invoice total for the affected pool. If you prefer, we can also create an invoice adjustment; credit memo is standard and provides an auditable reference.)
- Timeline: We can issue the credit memo by 2027-06-10, provided Auriga confirms the invoice basis by 6/7. The credit will appear as a reduction on the next paid statement and can be applied to the outstanding balance or future invoices per your preference.

Next steps for Auriga: please reply with either (A) confirmation that the prorated approach is acceptable and the May invoice line you want us to apply the 6% against, or (B) a request for an alternate remediation instrument (invoice offset). If you need a note from our legal team citing the exact SLA language, we can include that in the memo.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Finance Manager | Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com
